Adopt small-deformation, linear-elastic, homogeneous, isotropic Euler-Bernoulli beam mechanics under pure bending.
Assume plane sections remain plane and perpendicular to the deformed neutral axis.
Assume the neutral axis coincides with the centroidal axis of the rectangular cross-section.
Assume no contribution from axial force, transverse shear, or torsion to the normal bending stress at the section of interest.
Use a rectangular cross-section with width b = 50 mm and height h = 120 mm.
Compute the second moment of area about the centroidal neutral axis as I = b·h³/12 = 7.2 × 10⁶ mm⁴.
Take the distance from the neutral axis to the extreme fibers as c = h/2 = 60 mm.
Use the given internal bending moment at the cross-section M = 4.0 × 10⁶ N·mm, taken positive for sagging.
Define the fiber coordinate y measured from the neutral axis, with the positive y direction pointing upward (top fiber positive, bottom fiber negative).
Use the bending normal stress relation σ(y) = −M·y / I under this convention, so that for positive sagging M a positive y gives compression and a negative y gives tension.
Evaluate the bending stress at the neutral axis as σ(y = 0) = 0 MPa.
Evaluate the bending stress at the top fiber as σ(y = +60 mm) = −4.0 × 10⁶ × 60 / 7.2 × 10⁶ ≈ −33.33 MPa, i.e., compression.
Evaluate the bending stress at the bottom fiber as σ(y = −60 mm) = −4.0 × 10⁶ × (−60) / 7.2 × 10⁶ ≈ +33.33 MPa, i.e., tension.
Report the maximum bending stress magnitude as |σ_max| = M·c / I ≈ 33.33 MPa, occurring at the top and bottom extreme fibers with equal magnitude and opposite sign.
Keep all quantities in consistent SI-related units: force in N, length in mm, and stress in N/mm² = MPa.
